source_caption:
Girl, Interrupted (1999) is one of those movies that feels even more powerful when you learn how much of it came from real life.

The film is based on Susanna Kaysen’s 1993 memoir about the 18 months she spent at McLean Hospital in Massachusetts after a suicide attempt in 1967. Susanna is real, and many of the women she describes in the book were based on people she actually knew there.

Winona Ryder was deeply connected to the material. She discovered the book and spent years trying to get it made, eventually starring as Susanna and serving as an executive producer. Ryder had also experienced a brief hospitalization herself as a teenager, which made the story particularly personal to her. 

Angelina Jolie’s Lisa was inspired by a real woman Kaysen knew at McLean. The real woman had died before filming began, so Jolie couldn’t meet her or study her firsthand. Jolie later explained that she saw Lisa as someone who was simply being brutally honest rather than someone who thought she was “crazy.” 

Not everything in the movie actually happened, though. The filmmakers changed and combined events to create a more dramatic story. For example, several major scenes involving Daisy were significantly different from Kaysen’s memoir. 

And Jolie completely disappeared into Lisa. According to behind-the-scenes accounts, she even kept her distance from Ryder during filming because she felt that getting too close to her would make it harder to maintain Lisa’s detached personality. 

Jolie won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for the role.

More than 25 years later, Girl, Interrupted still feels deeply personal because underneath the drama, it came from someone’s actual experience of trying to understand herself.

Have you seen it?

source_details.synopsis: Girl, Interrupted is a 1999 American biographical drama film directed by James Mangold and written by Mangold, Lisa Loomer and Anna Hamilton Phelan, based on the 1993 memoir by Susanna Kaysen. Starring Winona Ryder, Angelina Jolie, Clea DuVall, Brittany Murphy, Elisabeth Moss, Jared Leto, Angela Bettis, Jeffrey Tambor, Vanessa Redgrave, and Whoopi Goldberg, the film follows a young woman who spends 18 months institutionalized at a psychiatric hospital following a suicide attempt. Girl, Interrupted was theatrically released in the United States on December 21, 1999, and grossed $48 million worldwide. It received mixed reviews, but Ryder, Jolie and Murphy were praised; Jolie won numerous award
